(11), citing Iwaniec-Kowalski). Independent numerics (my own code, scratchpad/lit_audit_verify.py, not the review's script): D1.3 verified at p=5 to machine precision (N(5)=1, S(5)=5^{5/2}, all five T_u = η(-1)G_Q(R(u)-1) with R=(2,0,5,2,1)); the Newton-identity reformulation (e_1..e_k all vanish iff p_1..p_k all vanish, triangularly, for k <= p-3 < p) verified at p=5,7,11,13 over 2000 random trials each — it is valid since each Newton step is k·e_k = (lower terms) with k invertible; and Moisio Cor 6.2 re-verified at q=p=5, m=5 (mP = 155,170,140 i.e. P = 31,34,28, matching the review's numbers exactly). Four independent searches with terminology the review did not use (Artin-Schreier trinomial degree-p perturbations; ker-of-trace twisted Kloosterman exact evaluation; Varshamov/self-reciprocal Russian-school; Salie/twisted-Kloosterman over extension fields with Frobenius exponents) found nothing containing the D1.3 object, and turned up one paper the review missed — Kolekar arXiv:2512.08994 (Dec 2025, irreducibles with coefficients in an affine algebraic set) — whose main theorem itself requires n < p and whose Question 5.1 explicitly lists p >= n as open, further corroborating that D1.3's regime (n = p) sits behind an explicitly acknowledged wall even in the newest work. The review's internal-circularity observation is algebraically correct (substituting S = η(-1)G_Q N into N = p^{-p}G_Q S gives N = p^{-p}η(-1)G_Q²N = N since G_Q² = η(-1)Q). Minor blemishes only: the review says existence 'is FALSE for 27% of primes' where D1_ATTACK.md records 61/238 = 25.6%; and its claim that the p=3 case IS a Salie sum is inherited from the workbench (structurally right since 2-p = -1 at p=3, but I did not independently recompute it). verdicts.claim: The Newton-identity reformulation (top coefficients x^{p-1}..x^3 vanish iff Tr(θ^k)=0 for k=1..p-3, valid since k<p) is correct
verdicts.reason: Checked myself as the task required: the k-th Newton identity gives k·e_k = Σ(-1)^{i-1}e_i p_{k-i} ... ± p_k with k invertible mod p for k ≤ p-3 < p, so (e_1..e_j)=0 iff (p_1..p_j)=0 triangularly for every j ≤ p-3; numerically verified over 2000 random polynomial trials each at p = 5, 7, 11, 13 with zero mismatches, including the per-prefix equivalence. Granger's §2.1 (Lemma 2, Eq. (5), re-retrieved) documents the same linear-triangular structure for k < p.
